sentence: This project builds an imaging probe to watch how immune cells called cytotoxic T-lymphocytes behave inside glioblastoma brain tumors.
This project studies how focused ultrasound changes activity in the macaque brain, using MRI and electrical recordings to check its effects and safety.
This project uses a polymer engineering technology to try to fix the limits of antibody-drug conjugates, which deliver toxic payloads to tumor cells.
This project builds a light sheet microscopy platform to image cells in every layer of the intestine, including immune and neuronal cells.
This project tries to improve how quickly and efficiently exogenic organs can be produced.
This project studies brain function and cognition in fragile X syndrome, from patients to animal experiments, to find markers of brain dysfunction and circuit mechanisms.
This project builds a nano-encapsulated manganese oxide contrast agent for MRI that tries to detect breast cancer left after chemotherapy more accurately.
This project studies how Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus enters human cells, multiplies in them, and causes disease in animals and humans.
This project uses stem cells to model how tendons develop and tries to find the regulators that help injured tendon repair itself.
This project studies how circadian rhythms in brain cells of the striatum affect craving and relapse to fentanyl and other opioids.
This project builds an algorithm that combines tissue and molecular markers to sort head and neck squamous cell carcinoma into high-risk and low-risk groups.
This project studies how childhood victimization and parenting change the way brain networks develop and how this relates to difficulty with emotion regulation.
This project tries to find out why ectodermal-neural cortex 1 makes some neurons more vulnerable to degeneration in early Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds tools to study Juberg-Marsidi syndrome, a rare developmental disorder linked to the HUWE1 gene, and how it arises.
This project uses computational modeling to study how electrodes record from and stimulate the human brain, including in deep brain stimulation.
This project studies whether the microbiome in early life plays a causal role in childhood obesity and asthma, using genetic and clinical data from children.
This project builds computer models of how pathogens and human cells interact, and uses deep learning to predict infectious disease outcomes.
This project builds a dental implant that delivers bone-forming stem cells to the gap between a loosened implant and the jawbone.
This project studies how peroxisomes and lipid droplets form in parts of the endoplasmic reticulum, using yeasts and mammalian cell culture.
This project makes vaccine proteins and measures immune responses to an HIV vaccine in rhesus macaques and humans, including B cells and antibodies.
